source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Neural Control and Coordination
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: At a chemical synapse, neurotransmitter is released from synaptic vesicles of the
questions.explanation: Ca2+ entry into the bouton triggers exocytosis of transmitter toward the synaptic cleft.

questions.stem: The resting membrane potential of a typical neuron is about
questions.explanation: The inside is negative (about -70 mV) because of the Na+/K+ pump and K+ leak.

questions.stem: The photoreceptors used for colour vision and concentrated at the fovea are
questions.explanation: Cones contain iodopsins and work in bright light; rods (rhodopsin) serve dim-light vision.

questions.stem: The insulating myelin sheath of a peripheral axon is formed by
questions.explanation: Schwann cells wrap PNS axons; oligodendrocytes myelinate CNS axons.

questions.stem: Balance, posture and fine timing of voluntary movement are chiefly functions of the
questions.explanation: The cerebellum compares intended and actual movement; medulla handles vital autonomic centres.

questions.stem: In a simple knee-jerk reflex the afferent neuron synapses in the
questions.explanation: The stretch reflex arc is completed in the spinal cord, often monosynaptically.

questions.stem: The sympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system is also called
questions.explanation: Sympathetic outflow leaves through thoracic and lumbar spinal nerves (fight-or-flight).

questions.stem: The organ of Corti, which converts sound vibrations into nerve impulses, rests on the
questions.explanation: Hair cells of the organ of Corti sit on the basilar membrane inside the cochlear duct.

questions.stem: The outermost tough meninx covering the brain is the
questions.explanation: Dura is outer, arachnoid middle, pia inner; CSF fills the subarachnoid space.

questions.stem: Saltatory conduction occurs because the action potential jumps from one
options: node of Ranvier to the next
Schwann nucleus to the axon hillock
questions.explanation: Myelin insulates internodes so current appears only at nodes, speeding conduction.

questions.stem: The neurotransmitter at the vertebrate neuromuscular junction is
questions.explanation: Acetylcholine binds nicotinic receptors on the muscle end-plate and is then split by acetylcholinesterase.

questions.stem: Depolarisation of an axon membrane is due mainly to rapid influx of
questions.explanation: Voltage-gated Na+ channels open and Na+ rushes in, reversing polarity toward +40 mV.

questions.stem: A person with a long eyeball focuses distant images in front of the retina. The defect and the correcting lens are
questions.explanation: Myopia (long eyeball or strong lens) is corrected by a diverging (concave) lens.

questions.stem: Which ion influx into the synaptic knob is immediately required for vesicle fusion?
questions.explanation: Presynaptic Ca2+ triggers SNARE-mediated release of neurotransmitter.

questions.stem: Repolarisation of the axon after a spike is caused mainly by
questions.explanation: Na+ channels inactivate and K+ efflux restores the negative inside.

questions.stem: The blind spot of the retina is the region where
options: the optic nerve leaves and photoreceptors are absent
only rods occur in a pit
questions.explanation: No rods or cones exist at the optic disc, so that point is insensitive to light.

questions.stem: Nissl granules in a neuron cell body are
options: rough ER with ribosomes for protein synthesis
questions.explanation: Nissl substance is RER; it is absent from the axon hillock and axon.

questions.stem: The hypothalamus is an important part of the
options: forebrain that controls homeostasis and the pituitary
questions.explanation: Hypothalamus (diencephalon) regulates temperature, hunger, thirst and endocrine output.

questions.stem: The correct order of a reflex arc is
options: receptor → sensory neuron → CNS → motor neuron → effector
questions.explanation: Afferent input enters the CNS; efferent output then drives the muscle or gland.

questions.stem: Parasympathetic stimulation typically
options: raises heart rate and dilates bronchi
slows heart rate and promotes digestion
is identical to the somatic system
arises only from the thoracic cord
questions.explanation: Craniosacral (rest-and-digest) outflow conserves energy; sympathetic does the opposite.

questions.stem: Semicircular canals detect
options: linear acceleration and static head position only
questions.explanation: Cristae in the ampullae sense rotation; maculae of utricle and saccule sense gravity and linear motion.

questions.stem: Cerebrospinal fluid is formed mainly by the
questions.explanation: Choroid plexus secretes CSF, which cushions the CNS and exchanges metabolites.

questions.stem: An electrical synapse differs from a chemical synapse in that the cells are coupled by
options: a wide cleft and slow diffusion of ACh
gap junctions that allow direct ion flow
questions.explanation: Gap junctions give almost no synaptic delay; chemical synapses use a cleft and transmitter.

questions.stem: Which statement about chemical synaptic transmission is incorrect?
options: Transmitter is stored in vesicles of the bouton
Receptors lie on the postsynaptic membrane
The impulse jumps the cleft as an electric spark without any chemical
Enzymes or reuptake clear transmitter from the cleft
questions.explanation: Chemical synapses use a messenger; they do not pass the spike as a spark across the cleft.

questions.stem: The Na+/K+ pump of the axon membrane
options: exchanges 2 Na+ out for 3 K+ in
exchanges 3 Na+ out for 2 K+ in and uses ATP
opens only during the peak of the spike
questions.explanation: The ATPase maintains gradients that make the resting potential and recovery possible.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect pair of eye defect and cause.
options: Myopia — image of a distant object in front of the retina
Hypermetropia — short eyeball or weak lens
Myopia — corrected by a convex converging lens
questions.explanation: Myopia needs a concave (diverging) lens; convex lenses correct hypermetropia.
